card: This PR optimizes HKDF expansion in CHKDF_HMAC_SHA256_L32 by caching the initialized CHMAC_SHA256 state and copying it on each expansion rather than rehashing the key pads. For BIP324 encrypted connection handshakes, which perform six expansions per session, this eliminates ten SHA-256 compressions, yielding a reported 20.6% throughput improvement in the HKDF microbenchmark. It also updates the API to enforce a fixed-size 32-byte output span at compile time.
evidence: Author benchmark BIP324_HKDF shows throughput increasing from 1,430,064 to 1,724,373 ops/s (+20.6%)
Commit 80130b90e2 notes saving ten SHA-256 compressions across BIP324's six expansions while keeping derived output bytes identical
problem: BIP324 v2 transport setup derives six values from a single HKDF context using the same secret. Each expansion was reinitializing HMAC from scratch with the pseudorandom key, executing two redundant SHA-256 block compressions each time. In addition, the previous array parameter decayed to a pointer, leaving room for buffer size mismatches.

risk.why: A flaw in HKDF key derivation would produce incorrect session keys and break BIP324 P2P connection handshakes.

scope_notes: Modifies internal cryptographic primitives and updates call sites to use std::span.
summary: Optimizes CHKDF_HMAC_SHA256_L32 by precomputing and storing the CHMAC_SHA256 state upon initialization rather than reinitializing HMAC on every expansion. Expansions copy the prepared HMAC state, avoiding repeated SHA-256 compressions over HMAC key pads. It also updates the HKDF API to use byte spans and enforce a compile-time fixed-size 32-byte output buffer.
